title: Set the buck's duty cycle
story: A buck converter runs from a 12 V battery at 100 kHz and must power a 5 V board that draws 1 A (a 5 ohm load). With ideal switches, its switch node is simply a square wave between 0 V and 12 V, drawn here as a pulse source. The inductor (100 uH) and capacitor (47 uF) are fitted. Choose the pulse source with the right duty cycle so the output sits between 4.8 V and 5.2 V after 4 ms.

goals.label: output between 4.8 V and 5.2 V at 4 ms

hints: In steady state the inductor's average voltage is zero, so the output equals the average of the switch node.
Vout = D x Vin. Solve for D.
The start-up overshoots and rings for about a millisecond; by 4 ms it has settled.
